findings.title: Lending, Credit and Finance (Amendment) Rules 2026 in Effect from 1 October
findings.summary: Guernsey's Lending, Credit and Finance (Amendment) Rules 2026 came into effect on 1 October 2026. Under the amendments, firms already licensed by the Guernsey Financial Services Commission will no longer be required to hold a separate virtual asset service provider (VASP) licence in every case where they wish to undertake virtual asset activity. The GFSC also launched a fees consultation for 2027 closing 6 October 2026.
findings.source_name: Mourant - Guernsey FinReg Quarterly Update Q3 2026

findings.title: AMLA Publishes Three Final Draft RTS on CDD and AML Cooperation Standards (1 October 2026)
findings.summary: On 1 October 2026, the EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) announced three final draft Regulatory Technical Standards (RTS), proposed to apply six months after their entry into force once adopted and published in the Official Journal of the EU. These standards cover customer due diligence (CDD) measures and triggers, and cooperation standards for AML supervisors. The standards are now in the Commission review and parliamentary process, expected to become binding law by January 2027.
findings.source_name: AMLR Explained – Didit / AMLA regulatory timeline

findings.title: Jersey Prospectus Requirements Updated – Amendment Orders in Force 30 September 2026
findings.summary: Changes to prospectus requirements under the Companies (General Provisions) (Jersey) Amendment Order 2026 and Companies Law (Jersey) Amendment Order 2026 came into force on 30 September 2026. Registrar consent will no longer apply to the circulation of prospectuses outside Jersey, making it easier for Jersey companies to operate internationally and reducing administrative duplication. This forms part of Jersey's Financial Services Competitiveness Programme ('Time to Win' action plan launched March 2026).
findings.source_name: Jersey Finance – Jersey Moves to Simplify its Financial Services Framework

findings.title: MAS Launches Consultation on Corporate Governance for Banks and Insurers (P016-2026)
findings.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) launched Consultation P016-2026 on 30 September 2026, seeking feedback on targeted updates to Corporate Governance Regulations for banks, insurers, and designated financial holding companies. Proposed changes address director independence, board composition, and appointment of key principals. The consultation closes 9 December 2026.
findings.source_name: MAS Media Release – Consultation on Corporate Governance Requirements

findings.title: CIMA Entity Removals Hit Record High in 2026 – 443 Entities Deregistered YTD
findings.summary: CIMA has removed 443 entities from its register in 2026 through early October, representing a 54% increase over the 287 removed in 2025 and the highest annual tally on record. The uptick comes as CIMA updates and digitises its fund deregistration process ahead of the Caribbean FATF evaluation in December 2027. CIMA also raised the Fund Annual Return (FAR) filing fee approximately 28% (CI$350 to CI$450 per fund annually).
findings.source_name: Cayman Compass – CIMA removals hit record high in 2026

findings.title: ADGM FSRA Publishes Fund Framework Amendments – Effective 16 September 2026
findings.summary: On 16 September 2026, the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) Financial Services Regulatory Authority (FSRA) published and immediately enacted amendments to several key Rules governing its funds framework. This follows a consultation paper (No. 12 of 2025) proposing enhancements. Separately, the DIFC's Dubai Financial Services Authority (DFSA) recently closed consultation on a comprehensive overhaul of its own funds regime.
findings.source_name: Akin Gump – Recent Changes to ADGM and DIFC Funds Framework

findings.title: BCB Resolution 561 – Stablecoin Cross-Border Remittance Ban in Force from 1 October 2026
findings.summary: Banco Central do Brasil (BCB) Resolution 561 (published 30 April 2026) bars payment firms from settling cross-border remittances in crypto, including dollar-pegged stablecoins, effective 1 October 2026. Additionally, the deadline for existing VASPs to apply for BCB authorisation is 30 October 2026; after that date, banks and financial institutions may not provide services to unauthorised crypto companies.
findings.source_name: FCM Law – Brazil VASP Licence: BCB Rules, Deadlines and FAQ (2026)

findings.title: Supplementary Law 227/2026 – ITCMD Now Applies to Overseas Assets at Market Value
findings.summary: In January 2026, Supplementary Law No. 227/2026 introduced mandatory valuation of inherited or gifted assets at market value (previously not required), substantially increasing succession costs in Brazil. Critically, the law also makes it possible to levy Brazilian ITCMD (inheritance and gift tax) on overseas assets, where tax jurisdiction is determined by the nature and location of assets. This represents a fundamental shift for cross-border estate planning involving Brazilian beneficiaries.
findings.source_name: Chambers Private Wealth 2026 – Brazil

findings.title: Cayman Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2026 – Legitimate Interest Access Model, Expanded Coverage
findings.summary: The Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2026 expanded entity coverage (private/mutual funds and trust structures now subject to disclosure requirements), lowered reporting obligations, and introduced a 'legitimate interest' access model rather than a fully public register. Access requires demonstrating legitimate interest and paying a CI$250 annual fee (single search raised from $30 to $75). Cayman resisted UK pressure for a fully public 'Google-style' register.
findings.source_name: Global Law Experts – Cayman Islands Beneficial Ownership Reforms 2026

findings.title: BVI Beneficial Ownership Register – Legitimate Interest Access Open from 1 April 2026; 10% Threshold
findings.summary: From 1 April 2026, the BVI Registry began accepting applications from persons demonstrating legitimate interest to access beneficial ownership information. A beneficial owner is now defined at the 10% ownership or control threshold (down from 25%), bringing more individuals within scope. Disclosures on legitimate interest access are limited to individuals with 25%+ ownership: name, nationality, month/year of birth, and nature of interest.
findings.source_name: Harneys – BVI Beneficial Ownership Information Updates

findings.title: FinCEN Final Rule – BOI Reporting Permanently Eliminated for US Domestic Companies (August 2026)
findings.summary: On 11 August 2026 (effective 14 August 2026), FinCEN issued a final rule permanently removing the requirement for US domestic companies and US persons to report beneficial ownership information under the Corporate Transparency Act. No domestic entity—regardless of size—has any BOI reporting obligation. Foreign reporting companies registered to do business in the US remain subject to BOI requirements. Previously-filed BOI for US persons will be deleted from the database.
findings.source_name: Mayer Brown – FinCEN Permanently Eliminates BOI Reporting for US Companies

findings.title: Florida SB 264 Foreign Buyer Real Estate Restrictions – Upheld November 2025, Ongoing Compliance
findings.summary: Florida's Senate Bill 264 restricting real estate purchases by foreign principals from seven 'countries of concern' (China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, Syria, Venezuela's Maduro regime) was upheld by courts in November 2025. All buyers must sign compliance affidavits at closing. Chinese-connected buyers face the broadest restrictions on any Florida real property. Violations carry property forfeiture and felony charges.
findings.source_name: South Florida Law PLLC – Foreign Real Estate Buyer Restrictions in Florida

findings.title: Luxembourg 2026 Budget: New Carried Interest Tax Regime, SPF Reform, and Start-up Tax Credit
findings.summary: Luxembourg introduced a new carried interest tax regime from tax year 2026: carried interest in an AIF is exempt from tax if the participation has been held more than six months and represents no more than 10% of fund share capital. Private wealth companies (SPFs) may now be established as simplified joint-stock companies. A new 20% income tax credit (capped at €100k per investor/year) applies to investments in eligible start-ups with a minimum €10k per start-up.
findings.source_name: Ogier – Luxembourg Tax Update: What's New in 2026

findings.title: MAS Circular AMLD 05/2026 – Risk-Proportionate Source of Wealth Guidance (25 May 2026)
findings.summary: On 25 May 2026, the Monetary Authority of Singapore issued Circular AMLD 05/2026 setting out how financial institutions in wealth management should establish a customer's Source of Wealth (SOW) in a risk-proportionate manner. The guidance operationalises Singapore's updated AML framework effective January 2026 and is particularly relevant for private banks, family offices, and asset managers.
findings.source_name: Alpadis – MAS Source of Wealth Guidance

findings.title: FINMA Consults on Revised AML Ordinance (12 May 2026) – FATF Preparation
findings.summary: On 12 May 2026, FINMA launched a consultation on the partially revised Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance to implement higher-ranking federal law, address FATF criticisms ahead of Switzerland's fifth FATF evaluation in 2027, and strengthen the integrity of Switzerland's financial centre. New rules would require financial intermediaries to identify the natural person behind every complex corporate structure. The UK-Switzerland Berne Financial Services Agreement (BFSA) entered into force 1 January 2026, facilitating cross-border private banking services.
findings.source_name: FinCrime Central – Swiss Regulator FINMA Updates AML Standards for 2026

findings.title: Panama Decree 25/2026 – FATCA/CRS Controlling Person Threshold Reduced to 10%
findings.summary: In June 2026, Panama's Ministry of Economy and Finance published Decree No. 25, reducing the ownership/control threshold for reportable controlling persons under FATCA and CRS from 25% to 10%. The decree also allows reporting financial institutions to rely on AML/KYC procedures (treating trust settlors and foundation founders as controlling persons). SBP Rule 1-2026 additionally requires enhanced beneficial ownership declarations for FinTech entities.
findings.source_name: KPMG Tax News Flash – Panama: Ownership Threshold Reduced under FATCA and CRS

findings.title: OECD Pillar Two – Administrative Guidance on Side-by-Side Arrangements and UTPR Safe Harbour
findings.summary: In May 2026, the OECD provided further Pillar Two updates including: administrative guidance on late-filing penalties for jurisdictions implementing the Global Minimum Tax from 2024; further guidance on the Transitional UTPR Safe Harbour for 52-53-week fiscal years; and an update to the Central Record for qualifying-status jurisdictions. The Inclusive Framework agreed on core elements of a Side-by-Side arrangement with safe harbours for MNEs headquartered in eligible-regime jurisdictions.
findings.source_name: Deloitte – OECD Pillar Two Global Minimum Tax

findings.title: CRS BRS Version 3.0.0-17 Applicable from 1 March 2026 – New Account Holder Data Fields
findings.summary: Technical standard BRS Version 3.0.0-17 for AEOI (CRS/FATCA) became applicable from 1 March 2026, aligned with CRS XML Schema V.3. New data fields added cover equity interest type, self-certification, account number type, account type, due diligence procedure, joint account indicators, and controlling person type. The UK separately expanded CRS scope to include electronic money institutions and introduced mandatory financial institution registration.
findings.source_name: SARS – Automatic Exchange of Information BRS AEOI: CRS & FATCA

findings.title: UAE Onshore Change-of-Control Notification/Clearance Regime Established (2026)
findings.summary: In 2026, UAE onshore legislation established a new regime requiring notification or clearance for changes of control in onshore licensed financial entities, aligning with existing DIFC and ADGM requirements. This affects mergers, acquisitions, and restructurings of UAE-regulated wealth management firms, funds, and financial institutions.
findings.source_name: Mondaq – UAE Change of Control Rules for Regulated Financial Businesses

findings.title: Cyprus FDI Screening Law in Effect from 2 April 2026
findings.summary: The Republic of Cyprus' new Foreign Direct Investment Screening Law came into force on 2 April 2026, introducing look-back provisions, a defined screening remit, internal change trigger points, and notification requirements with relatively low thresholds. The law reshaped the investment landscape for foreign investors acquiring interests in Cypriot entities.
findings.source_name: White & Case – Foreign Direct Investment Reviews 2026

findings.title: Isle of Man – Financial Services (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill Consultation Open
findings.summary: The Isle of Man Financial Services Authority (IOMFSA) is consulting on the Financial Services (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill, proposing a package of amendments to modernise and strengthen financial services legislation. Areas covered include enforcement, civil penalties, warning notices, appeal rights, inspection and investigation powers, guidance provisions, fees, public statements, and broader regulatory consistency. The IOMFSA is collaborating with Guernsey and Jersey on a joint Crown Dependencies framework for Authorised Push Payment (APP) fraud prevention.
findings.source_name: Isle of Man Government – Financial Services (Miscellaneous Provisions) Bill Consultation

findings.title: FIRPTA – 15% Withholding Rate Applies to Foreign Sellers of US Real Property in 2026
findings.summary: FIRPTA withholding on foreign sellers of US real property remains at 15% in 2026 (increased from 10% under prior Congressional action), except for personal residences with a sale price not exceeding $1 million. Treasury and IRS released final regulations under Section 892 in December 2025 governing foreign government investment. The FIRPTA exemption for domestically controlled REITs was finalised in April 2024 and is fully operative in 2026.
findings.source_name: Home Abroad Inc – FIRPTA Guide: Foreign Investors in US Property

findings.title: Jersey Control of Borrowing (Amendment) Order 2026 – Streamlining Regulatory Scope
findings.summary: The Control of Borrowing (Jersey) Amendment Order 2026 streamlines Jersey's regulatory framework by removing COBO consent requirements for shares, securities, and ownership interests issued by Jersey entities and certain non-Jersey entities raising money or having interests registered in Jersey. Subject to States Assembly approval, COBO controls relating to international capital raises will be largely eliminated, improving Jersey's competitiveness as a fund domicile.
findings.source_name: Appleby – Streamlining of Regulatory Scope in Jersey: COBO Amendment Order 2026
